# Threat Model — cloudmate.onrender.com (baseline, pre-recon)

**Status: provisional.** This baseline is derived from scan scope only (single web application target, hosted on Render.com). Recon output will replace inferred claims; agents should amend rather than re-derive.

## Overview
- Target: `https://cloudmate.onrender.com/` — a single web application (name suggests a cloud management/console-type product). Hosted on Render (PaaS), which implies a standard HTTPS web front-end, likely a Node/Python backend, with no direct infra access.
- Engagement type: black-box external assessment. No source code provided.
- Only this host is in scope. No subdomain expansion, no other Render accounts, no infrastructure testing beyond the HTTP(S) application layer.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions (inferred)
- **Internet → app**: unauthenticated attacker can reach all public routes. Anything not behind auth is attacker-reachable.
- **Authenticated user → app**: unknown auth model yet (login form, roles, tenants) — to be filled by recon.
- **App → third parties**: unknown (OAuth, payment, email integrations possible).
- Assumption: the app has an authenticated user boundary of some kind; if it is a demo/sandbox app with public demo data, severity of data-exposure findings drops accordingly.

## Attack Surface (to be enumerated)
- Public web pages, client-side JS bundles, API endpoints (`/api/*` or similar), auth flows, file uploads if any.
- Render-specific: no direct infra access (no port scanning of Render infra beyond the HTTP service itself).

## Severity Calibration
- Critical: unauth RCE, full auth bypass, mass cross-user/tenant data access.
- High: SQLi reaching data, SSRF to internal services, object-level authz failures on sensitive data, stored XSS on high-value surfaces.
- Medium: reflected XSS, CSRF on state-changing actions, lower-value authz gaps.
- Low/Info: headers, verbose errors, enumeration.
- Demo-content caveat: if the app serves only public demo data with no real accounts, confidentiality findings are downgraded; auth-bypass findings remain high because the control is still broken.

## Attacker Stories (initial)
- Unauth attacker reaches admin or internal endpoints by guessing paths.
- Authenticated low-priv user accesses other users' objects via IDOR.
- Injection in any input reflected to a server-side sink.
